name: Ruxolitinib oral
lead: Ruxolitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK1/JAK2) inhibitor developed by Incyte and sold orally as Jakafi in the United States and Jakavi elsewhere (Novartis).[1] Its approved oral indications are blood and transplant conditions, namely myelofibrosis, polycythemia vera and graft-versus-host disease; a topical cream (Opzelura) is approved for atopic dermatitis and vitiligo.[1]

Oral ruxolitinib is not approved for alopecia areata. It is discussed in hair-loss contexts because JAK inhibitors as a class have been studied for that autoimmune condition, and Wikipedia lists alopecia areata only as an area under investigation.[1][2]
Because it is a systemic immunomodulating drug, reviews of JAK inhibitors in dermatology discuss infection and cancer risks for the class.[2][3]

paras: Oral ruxolitinib is approved for intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis (FDA, November 2011), polycythemia vera (2014), steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease (2019) and chronic graft-versus-host disease (2021).[1]

Reported adverse effects in its approved indications include low platelet, red cell and neutrophil counts, urinary tract infections, bleeding, bruising, weight gain, raised cholesterol, dizziness, headache and elevated liver enzymes; herpes zoster and opportunistic infections have also been reported.[1] Narrative reviews of cancer risk with JAK inhibitors in dermatology discuss concerns about malignancy and opportunistic infection across the class.[3]

Ruxolitinib selectively inhibits JAK1 and JAK2, which recruit STAT proteins to cytokine receptors and thereby modulate gene expression.[1] The JAK-STAT pathway is central to several immune-mediated skin diseases.[2]

No studies found for oral ruxolitinib in alopecia areata among the sources reviewed for this article; Wikipedia describes that use as under investigation, without results.[1] Registered trials of oral ruxolitinib concern hematologic malignancies, myelofibrosis, graft-versus-host disease and COVID-19.[4][5][6]

timeline.event: FDA approves oral ruxolitinib for myelofibrosis.[1]
Approval for steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease.[1]
Topical ruxolitinib approved for atopic dermatitis.[1]

card.summary: Oral JAK inhibitor approved for blood and transplant disorders, only investigational for alopecia areata.
card.note: Systemic immunosuppressive prescription drug; not approved for hair loss.

quick.overview:
Oral ruxolitinib (Jakafi) is a prescription JAK inhibitor approved for myelofibrosis, polycythemia vera and graft-versus-host disease.

Alopecia areata is described as an area of investigation, but the sources reviewed here contain no results for it. Other JAK inhibitors have approvals or trial data in that condition.
quick.mechanism: It blocks JAK1 and JAK2 enzymes that relay cytokine signals inside immune cells.
quick.risks: Reported effects include low blood counts, infections including shingles, raised cholesterol and liver enzymes. Reviews discuss cancer and infection concerns for the JAK inhibitor class. Prescription only.
